newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tanker chartering lifts, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tanker chartering lifts, rates steady.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering activity in the key Middle East Gulf market rose slightly from the previous day's lull, London brokers said on Friday.
Other lifting sectors saw unchanged freight rates.
Although no ULCC chartering was seen, three VLCCs found employment, all eastwards bound.
VLCCs heading for Japan were again fixed at last done levels of W64. Western voyages commanded W53 whilst rates for VLCCs travelling east ascended slowly to W62.5 from Thursday's W60.
"There are a lot of cargoes still to be lifted in September and there is no doubt that some charterers are holding back in the hope that rates will fall next week," one broker commented.
"There are a few owners out there who must be feeling slightly nervous at the moment," he continued.

Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med remained on an equilibrium of W92.5, amidst a dearth of charter activity. Later on Friday not a single vessel had been seen. Brokers were unable to suggest a reason for this.
In the inter-UKC sector, rates were seen as a touch softer at W94, brokers estimated.
Caribbean rates were a touch softer as evidenced by Phillips' chartering of the 70,000 tonner, Pioneer, travelling from Puerto La Cruz. Rates were off W2.5 at W127.5.
